Answer: D
Reason: The imaging sequence demonstrates a rapid progression from initial interstitial opacities to severe bilateral alveolar consolidations, followed by complete resolution on follow-up X-rays (Figures 5a and 5b), which is characteristic of Weil Syndrome (severe leptospirosis) and distinguishes it from conditions like Goodpasture syndrome or crack lung that typically leave residual fibrosis or have different clinical courses.
